must_fix.title: Keyboard focus ring on the selected genre chip has ~1.1:1 contrast and is effectively invisible
must_fix.evidence: css/styles.css: `:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus) }` (#1d5c7a) is drawn fully inside `.chip:has(input:checked) { background: var(--accent) }` (#8a3416). Roving focus in a radio group always lands on the checked radio. Playwright probe focusing input[value="Classics"] at 360px: `[ 'Classics', 'rgb(29, 92, 122)', 'solid', 'rgb(138, 52, 22)' ]`; contrast calc: `focus on accent 1.1086506041587085` (vs 7.2:1 on unselected chips). Fails WCAG 1.4.11 (3:1) for the issue's accessibility requirement; tests/accessibility.test.js:86 only checks outline style/width so it doesn't catch it.

nits: Home page title order 'Marginalia Books | Home' differs from the other pages' 'X | Marginalia Books'.
Checked chip uses accent-color equal to its own background, so the radio's ring blends into the chip (fill and text colour still show the selection).
tests/accessibility.test.js:3 refers to 'Criterion 8' from a spec not in the repo.

report:
This PR isn't ready to merge: it needs one accessibility fix before it goes in. On the books page, the keyboard focus ring on the genre filter is almost invisible.

**Checks run**
- `NODE_PATH=/opt/node-tools/node_modules npm test` → `# tests 59 # pass 59 # fail 0`. The repo has no lint or format config, so there were no other checks to run.
- At 360px and at 320px, every page has `scrollWidth == innerWidth`, so nothing scrolls sideways. This includes `books.html?genre=Classics`. No page logged console or network errors.
- The filter behaves correctly:
  - Arrow keys move through the genres and update the URL.
  - The back button restores the previous genre.
  - `?genre=Poetry%20%26%20Essays` shows 3 books.
  - `?genre=bogus` falls back to All (15 of 15).
- The contact form, nav, landmarks, the 8+ title requirement (15 books) and the "no external requests" requirement all hold up.

**Must fix: the focus ring disappears on a selected genre chip**
- In `css/styles.css`, focused elements get a blue outline (`--focus: #1d5c7a`).
- A selected chip is filled with the brand rust colour (`.chip:has(input:checked) { background: var(--accent) }`, accent `#8a3416`).
- The radio's outline sits 3px out from a 24px radio, inside a chip at least 44px tall. So it is drawn entirely on the rust fill.
- In a radio group, keyboard focus always lands on the selected radio. So this is the focus state keyboard users see every time they reach the filter.
- Measured with Playwright, focusing `input[value="Classics"]` at 360px:
  `[ 'Classics', 'rgb(29, 92, 122)', 'solid', 'rgb(138, 52, 22)' ]`
- Contrast of the outline against the chip: `focus on accent 1.1086506041587085`. Against an unselected chip it is about 7.2:1.
- WCAG 1.4.11 requires 3:1 for focus indicators, so 1.1:1 fails the issue's "accessible" requirement. A screenshot confirms the ring is barely visible.
- The existing test (`tests/accessibility.test.js:86`) misses this because it only checks that an outline style and width exist, not its colour against the background. A test for the fix should check that contrast.

**Nits**
- The home page title is `Marginalia Books | Home`, but the other pages use `Books | Marginalia Books`. The order is inconsistent.
- A selected chip uses `accent-color: var(--accent)` on an accent background, so the radio's own ring blends into the chip. The fill and text colour still show which genre is selected.
- `tests/accessibility.test.js:3` refers to "Criterion 8", which comes from a spec that isn't in the repo.

My probe scripts were in the session scratchpad, outside the repo, and `git status` is the same as when I started.
